question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the powers and multiply the two functions, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }({p}^{3}(x)\cdot {q}^{2}(x)) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }({(p(x))}^{3}\cdot {(q(x))}^{2}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }({(-3{x}^{3})}^{3}\cdot {(-3{x}^{3})}^{2}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(-27{x}^{9}\cdot 9{x}^{6}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }((-27\cdot 9){x}^{9+6}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(-243\cdot {x}^{15}) \\  & =-243\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{15}\end{aligned}
$$

The graph $y={x}^{15}$ is power function with an odd positive power and therefore has the property that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{15}=\infty .
$$

Multiplication by the negative constant $-243$ changes the sign of the limit. 
So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned} & =-243\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{15} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{15} \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }(-243{x}^{15})=-\infty .
$$
